```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Eloot_2016_urea"))$reference`
* Article: [PLoS One 2016;11(1):e0147159](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0147159) (open access)

Eloot et al. measured urea and five protein-bound uremic solutes during one
midweek high-flux hemodialysis session in ten patients and, separately for each
solute, fitted a two-compartment kinetic model (their Fig 1, Eq. 1-2):

* a plasmatic compartment `V1`, directly accessible to the dialyzer, into which
  the solute is generated at a constant rate `G`;
* an extraplasmatic compartment `V2 = Vtot - V1`, exchanging with plasma by an
  intercompartment clearance `K21`;
* removal from plasma by the dialyzer clearance `K` while a session runs;
* net ultrafiltration `QUF` shrinking both volumes in proportion to their size.

The calibrated models were then used to compare seven dialysis schedules
(Table 1) by total solute removal (TSR), steady-state time-averaged
concentration (TAC1) and steady-state predialysis concentration (C1_pre)
(Table 4). nlmixr2lib packages one model per solute:

```{r models}
solutes <- c(
  urea = "Eloot_2016_urea",
  PCG = "Eloot_2016_pCresylGlucuronide",
  HA = "Eloot_2016_hippuricAcid",
  IAA = "Eloot_2016_indoleAceticAcid",
  IS = "Eloot_2016_indoxylSulfate",
  PCS = "Eloot_2016_pCresylSulfate"
)
mods <- lapply(solutes, function(nm) rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(nm)))
data.frame(
  abbreviation = names(solutes),
  model = unname(solutes),
  protein_binding = c("0%", "13%", "47%", "73%", "93%", "95%")
) |>
  dplyr::rename("Solute" = abbreviation, "Model" = model, "Protein binding (Table 2)" = protein_binding) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

PCG = p-cresylglucuronide, HA = hippuric acid, IAA = indole acetic acid,
IS = indoxyl sulfate, PCS = p-cresylsulfate.

# Population

Ten stable patients on chronic thrice-weekly 4-h high-flux hemodialysis at
Ghent University Hospital (2 women, 8 men), aged 69 +/- 12 years, body weight
75.0 [69.9;82.6] kg, 50 [30;62] months on dialysis, residual renal function
2.6 [0.4;3.8] mL/min, hematocrit 37.2 +/- 4.2% and total plasma protein
61.4 +/- 6.4 g/L. The study session lasted 240 min with blood and dialysate
flows of 300 and 700 mL/min and ultrafiltration of 0.41 +/- 0.29 L/h
(Methods, "Patients"). The same information is stored in each model's
`population` metadata.

# Source trace

Every model shares one structure; only the six estimated values differ.

| Model element | Source location |
|---|---|
| Two-compartment structure, generation into `V1`, dialyzer clearance out of `V1` | Fig 1 |
| Mass balances `d(V1 C1)/dt = G - K C1 + K21 (C2 - C1)`, `d(V2 C2)/dt = -K21 (C2 - C1)` | Eq. 1-2 |
| Ultrafiltration distributed over both compartments in proportion to their volumes | Methods, "Calculations and kinetic modeling" |
| Both compartments start at the measured predialysis plasma concentration | Methods, "Calculations and kinetic modeling" |
| Dialyzer clearance constant through the session | Methods, "Calculations and kinetic modeling" |
| `lksyn` (G), `lcl_hemodialysis` (K), `lrbase` (Cpre) | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (V1), `lvp` (Vtot - V1), `lq` (K21) | Table 3 |
| `qpfr` (QUF = 0.41 L/h) | Methods, "Patients" |
| `qgain` (interdialytic regain) | Not printed; derived so the weekly fluid balance is zero (see Assumptions) |
| Strategy definitions (session count, length, blood flow, QUF, extraction ratio) | Table 1 and Methods, "Kinetic analysis to determine optimal removal" |
| Validation targets TSR, TAC1, C1_pre | Table 4 |

```{r ini-values}
ini_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(mods), function(ab) {
  ini <- mods[[ab]]$iniDf
  v <- stats::setNames(ini$est, ini$name)
  data.frame(
    solute = ab,
    G = exp(v[["lksyn"]]),
    K = exp(v[["lcl_hemodialysis"]]) * 1000,
    V1 = exp(v[["lvc"]]),
    Vtot = exp(v[["lvc"]]) + exp(v[["lvp"]]),
    K21 = exp(v[["lq"]]) * 1000,
    Cpre = exp(v[["lrbase"]])
  )
}))
ini_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Solute" = solute, "G (mg/min)" = G, "K (mL/min)" = K, "V1 (L)" = V1,
    "Vtot (L)" = Vtot, "K21 (mL/min)" = K21, "Cpre (mg/L)" = Cpre
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

# Calibration session

Figure 2 of the paper shows measured plasma concentrations and the fitted
plasmatic (C1) and extraplasmatic (C2) profiles of one representative patient.
The packaged models carry the typical values, so the curves below are the
typical patient rather than that individual: one 240-min session starting from
the predialysis concentration, with ultrafiltration at 0.41 L/h.

```{r calibration}
cal_events <- data.frame(
  id = 1L,
  time = 0:240,
  evid = 0L,
  amt = 0,
  cmt = "central",
  RRT_HEMODIAL_ACTIVE = 1
)
cal <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(mods), function(ab) {
  r <- rxode2::rxSolve(mods[[ab]], events = cal_events, returnType = "data.frame")
  data.frame(solute = ab, time = r$time, C1 = r$Cc, C2 = r$Cp, fluid = r$fluid_balance)
}))
cal$solute <- factor(cal$solute, levels = names(solutes))
```

```{r fig2, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Replicates the layout of Figure 2 of Eloot 2016 (typical patient, not the paper's representative individual): plasmatic C1 (bold) and extraplasmatic C2 (thin) during one 240-min session."}
cal |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(C1, C2), names_to = "compartment", values_to = "conc") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, linewidth = compartment)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(C1 = 1.2, C2 = 0.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~solute, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time since start of dialysis (min)", y = "Concentration (mg/L)", linewidth = NULL)
```

The paper's qualitative finding, a markedly slower decline in the
extraplasmatic compartment for every solute, holds for every model, and the
session removes 0.41 L/h x 4 h = 1.64 L of fluid:

```{r calibration-checks}
cal_end <- cal |>
  dplyr::group_by(solute) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    rr_C1 = 1 - C1[time == 240] / C1[time == 0],
    rr_C2 = 1 - C2[time == 240] / C2[time == 0],
    fluid_end = fluid[time == 240]
  )
knitr::kable(cal_end, digits = 3)
stopifnot(
  all(cal_end$rr_C1 > cal_end$rr_C2),
  all(cal_end$rr_C2 > 0),
  # Fluid removed in one session is exactly QUF x 240 min.
  all(abs(cal_end$fluid_end + 0.41 / 60 * 240) < 1e-6)
)
```

# Dialysis strategies (Table 4)

## Simulation design

Table 1 defines seven schedules. Sessions start at the same clock time on
Monday, Wednesday and Friday (thrice weekly) or Monday to Saturday (six times
weekly). For a blood flow of 150 mL/min the paper scales the extraction ratio by
1.33 for urea and 1.00 for the protein-bound solutes; since dialyzer clearance
is the extraction ratio times the flow, the clearance at 150 mL/min is
`0.5 x 1.33 = 0.665` times the 300-mL/min clearance for urea and `0.5` times it
for the protein-bound solutes. The ultrafiltration rate is set so that the
weekly fluid removal equals the 3 x 4 h reference (Table 1 `QUF` column), and
`qgain` returns the same volume between sessions. These three quantities are
the only parameters a strategy changes, and they are passed to `rxSolve()` as
parameter overrides.

As in the paper, each strategy starts from the steady state of the 3 x 4 h
schedule. TSR is the solute collected in the first session of the new schedule
(the sum of the first two sessions for six-times-weekly schedules), and TAC1 and
C1_pre are taken once the new steady state is reached. The switch is made at the
start of a Wednesday session, the midweek session the model was calibrated on,
and C1_pre is the concentration before the Wednesday session in the steady-state
week.

```{r strategy-functions}
week <- 10080
n_weeks <- 10

strategies <- data.frame(
  strategy = c(
    "3x4h_300/w", "3x8h_150/w", "6x4h_150/w", "6x2h_300/w",
    "3x8h_300/w", "6x4h_300/w", "6x8h_150/w"
  ),
  n = c(3, 3, 6, 6, 3, 6, 6),
  dur = c(240, 480, 240, 120, 480, 240, 480),
  qb = c(300, 150, 150, 300, 300, 300, 150)
)
strategies$blood_volume <- strategies$n * strategies$dur * strategies$qb / 1000

# Session start times (min) when the solve starts `offset` minutes after a
# Monday session start.
session_starts <- function(n, n_weeks, offset = 0) {
  day <- if (n == 3) c(0, 2, 4) else 0:5
  st <- as.vector(outer(day * 1440, (0:n_weeks) * week, "+")) - offset
  sort(st[st >= 0 & st < n_weeks * week])
}

make_events <- function(n, dur, n_weeks, init = NULL, offset = 0) {
  st <- session_starts(n, n_weeks, offset)
  tt <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, n_weeks * week, by = 10), st, st + dur)))
  on <- vapply(tt, function(x) any(x >= st & x < st + dur), logical(1))
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = tt, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central",
    RRT_HEMODIAL_ACTIVE = as.numeric(on)
  )
  if (!is.null(init)) {
    # evid = 5 replaces the compartment amounts with the 3 x 4 h steady state.
    ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
      data.frame(
        id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 5L, amt = unname(init), cmt = names(init),
        RRT_HEMODIAL_ACTIVE = 1
      ),
      ev
    )
  }
  ev
}

strategy_params <- function(mod, s, is_urea) {
  ini <- mod$iniDf
  lk <- ini$est[ini$name == "lcl_hemodialysis"]
  kfac <- if (s$qb == 150) (if (is_urea) 0.5 * 1.33 else 0.5) else 1
  quf <- 0.41 / 60 * 12 / (s$n * s$dur / 60)
  c(
    lcl_hemodialysis = lk + log(kfac),
    qpfr = quf,
    qgain = quf * s$n * s$dur / (week - s$n * s$dur)
  )
}

summarise_run <- function(r, n, dur, n_weeks, offset) {
  st <- session_starts(n, n_weeks, offset)
  collected <- function(t) r$dialysate[match(t, r$time)]
  first <- st[seq_len(if (n == 6) 2 else 1)]
  last_week <- r[r$time >= (n_weeks - 1) * week, ]
  c(
    TSR = sum(collected(first + dur) - collected(first)),
    TAC1 = sum(diff(last_week$time) *
      (head(last_week$Cc, -1) + tail(last_week$Cc, -1)) / 2) / week,
    C1_pre = r$Cc[match((n_weeks - 1) * week + 2 * 1440 - offset, r$time)],
    removed_last_week = collected(n_weeks * week) - collected((n_weeks - 1) * week)
  )
}
```

```{r strategy-simulation}
wednesday <- 2 * 1440
sim <- list()
for (ab in names(mods)) {
  mod <- mods[[ab]]
  ref <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = make_events(3, 240, n_weeks), returnType = "data.frame")
  t_switch <- (n_weeks - 1) * week + wednesday
  init <- c(
    central = ref$central[ref$time == t_switch],
    peripheral1 = ref$peripheral1[ref$time == t_switch]
  )
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(strategies))) {
    s <- strategies[i, ]
    r <- rxode2::rxSolve(
      mod,
      params = strategy_params(mod, s, ab == "urea"),
      events = make_events(s$n, s$dur, n_weeks, init, wednesday),
      returnType = "data.frame"
    )
    sim[[length(sim) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      solute = ab, strategy = s$strategy,
      t(summarise_run(r, s$n, s$dur, n_weeks, wednesday))
    )
  }
}
sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(sim)
# Table 4 reports urea in g and g/L, the other solutes in mg and mg/L.
urea_rows <- sim$solute == "urea"
sim[urea_rows, c("TSR", "TAC1", "C1_pre")] <- sim[urea_rows, c("TSR", "TAC1", "C1_pre")] / 1000
```

## Mass balance

Over the steady-state week the solute collected in the dialysate must equal the
solute generated, `G x 10080 min`:

```{r mass-balance}
mb <- sim |>
  dplyr::left_join(ini_tab[, c("solute", "G")], by = "solute") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (removed_last_week / (G * week) - 1))
stopifnot(all(abs(mb$pct_diff) < 0.5))
range(mb$pct_diff)
```

```{r table4}

    111, 126, 151, 139, 152, 185, 201,

  ),

    0.80, 0.62, 0.52, 0.71, 0.52, 0.40, 0.30,

)

cmp <- sim |>
  dplyr::select(solute, strategy, TSR, TAC1, C1_pre) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(TSR, TAC1, C1_pre), names_to = "metric", values_to = "simulated") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(paper, c(TSR, TAC1, C1_pre), names_to = "metric", values_to = "published"),
    by = c("solute", "strategy", "metric")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = published / simulated, pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / published - 1))

cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(solute = factor(solute, levels = names(solutes))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(solute, metric, strategy) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Solute" = solute, "Strategy" = strategy, "Metric" = metric,
    "Simulated" = simulated, "Published (Table 4)" = published,
    "Published / simulated" = ratio, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

The ratio of published to simulated values, summarised per solute over the 21
comparisons (7 strategies x 3 metrics):

```{r ratio-summary}
ratio_summary <- cmp |>
  dplyr::group_by(solute) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_ratio = median(ratio),
    cv_ratio_pct = 100 * sd(ratio) / mean(ratio),
    median_abs_pct_diff = median(abs(pct_diff)),
    max_abs_pct_diff = max(abs(pct_diff))
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(solute, names(solutes)))
knitr::kable(ratio_summary, digits = 3)
```

Two patterns are visible.

* **Urea, IAA, IS and PCS**, for which Tables 2 and 3 print the mean
  generation rate, reproduce Table 4 within 3-7% in the median and within
  20% for every strategy and metric. The paper simulated "the average
  dataset emanating out of our primary kinetic analysis", which need not
  coincide with the per-parameter means of individual fits, so close but not
  exact agreement is expected.
* **PCG and HA** are low by a near-constant factor (coefficient of variation
  of the ratio 2-3.5% across all 21 comparisons). For these two solutes
  Table 2 prints only the median generation rate with a right-skewed
  inter-quartile range. All three outputs are proportional to `G` in this linear
  model, so a constant ratio across strategies and metrics points to `G`: the
  paper's average dataset used a generation rate above the median. The implied
  rate, `median ratio x G`, lies inside the printed inter-quartile range. The
  packaged models keep the printed median (see Assumptions).

```{r table4-gates}
mean_g <- ratio_summary$solute %in% c("urea", "IAA", "IS", "PCS")
median_g <- ratio_summary$solute %in% c("PCG", "HA")
implied <- ini_tab |>
  dplyr::filter(solute %in% c("PCG", "HA")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(ratio_summary, by = "solute") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    G_implied = G * median_ratio,
    G_q1 = c(PCG = 0.016, HA = 0.123)[solute],
    G_q3 = c(PCG = 0.049, HA = 0.321)[solute]
  )
knitr::kable(implied[, c("solute", "G", "G_implied", "G_q1", "G_q3")], digits = 4)
stopifnot(
  # The model is deterministic, so these bounds are exact properties of the
  # packaged parameters rather than of a random cohort.
  all(abs(ratio_summary$median_abs_pct_diff[mean_g]) < 12),
  all(ratio_summary$max_abs_pct_diff[mean_g] < 25),
  all(ratio_summary$cv_ratio_pct[median_g] < 5),
  all(implied$G_implied > implied$G_q1 & implied$G_implied < implied$G_q3)
)
```

## Processed blood volume drives removal of strongly bound solutes

The paper's main conclusion is that, for strongly protein-bound solutes, the
weekly processed blood volume rather than the timeframe determines adequacy:
every 432-L/week schedule gives a lower TAC1 than every 216-L/week schedule.

```{r blood-volume}
bv <- sim |>
  dplyr::left_join(strategies[, c("strategy", "blood_volume")], by = "strategy") |>
  dplyr::filter(solute %in% c("IAA", "IS", "PCS")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(solute) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    max_TAC1_432L = max(TAC1[blood_volume == 432]),
    min_TAC1_216L = min(TAC1[blood_volume == 216])
  )
knitr::kable(bv, digits = 2)
stopifnot(all(bv$max_TAC1_432L < bv$min_TAC1_216L))
```

```{r fig4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Eloot 2016: TSR, TAC1 and C1_pre of hippuric acid and indoxyl sulfate for the seven strategies, simulated (bars) and published in Table 4 (points)."}
cmp |>
  dplyr::filter(solute %in% c("HA", "IS")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    strategy = factor(strategy, levels = strategies$strategy),
    metric = factor(metric, levels = c("TSR", "TAC1", "C1_pre"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(strategy, simulated)) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(y = published), colour = "black") +
  facet_grid(metric ~ solute, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "TSR (mg); TAC1 and C1_pre (mg/L)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Typical values only.** The paper fitted each patient separately and
  reports the between-patient mean +/- SD or median [IQR] of the individual
  estimates (Tables 2-3). It is not a population model, so the packaged models
  carry no between-subject or residual variability.
* **Mixed summary statistics.** Where a table prints a median rather than a
  mean (PCG and HA generation rate and predialysis concentration, PCG and PCS
  `Vtot`, IS `V1`), the median is used. `V2` is `Vtot - V1` from the printed
  values, so for PCG, IS and PCS it combines a median with a mean.
* **Generation rate of PCG and HA.** Table 4 implies a generation rate about
  1.6 (HA) and 1.8 (PCG) times the printed median, consistent with the mean of
  a right-skewed distribution. The mean is not printed; the models keep the
  median and do not back-solve it from Table 4.
* **Urea predialysis concentration unit.** Table 2 prints urea `Cpre` as 0.95
  under a mg/dL header. A urea level of 9.5 mg/L is not physiological for a
  dialysis patient, and the paper's own Table 4 gives a predialysis urea of
  1.13 g/L for the same schedule. The value is read as 0.95 g/L (950 mg/L).
* **Concentration units.** Table 2 reports concentrations in mg/dL; the models
  use mg/L (the unit of Table 4) and the source-trace comments show the factor
  of 10.
* **Interdialytic fluid regain.** The paper states that ultrafiltration
  shrinks both volumes but not how the fluid returns between sessions. The
  models restore it at the constant rate `qgain`, which equals the weekly
  ultrafiltrate of the 3 x 4 h schedule (0.41 L/h x 12 h) spread over the
  156 interdialytic hours. The paper keeps weekly weight loss the same across
  strategies, so the strategies above reset `qgain` for their own interdialytic
  time.
* **Ultrafiltration at the cohort mean.** `qpfr` is fixed at the cohort mean
  of 0.41 L/h. Users with patient-specific ultrafiltration should override it
  (and `qgain`).
* **Residual renal function** (median 2.6 mL/min) was not part of the paper's
  model and is not included.
* **Session timing.** The paper does not give clock times. Sessions start at
  the same time of day; TSR is the first session after a Wednesday switch and
  C1_pre is the Wednesday predialysis concentration. With a Monday switch the
  first-session TSR is about 25% higher for urea, because the long interdialytic
  interval precedes it, while TAC1 and C1_pre are unchanged.
* **External validation not reproduced.** Fig 5 compares the model with
  reduction ratios from Meijers et al., Sirich et al. and the group's own
  4 h / 8 h HD and HDF cross-over study. The dialyzer clearances,
  ultrafiltration rates and predialysis concentrations of those studies are not
  given in this paper, so that comparison is not repeated here.
